references.text: Concerns the purchase of a Hebrew slave and the conditions of his service, providing background for rules on treating Israelite slaves.
Parallel law regarding Hebrew slaves who sell themselves, with instructions for release in the seventh year and generosity upon liberation.
Exhorts not to view the freeing of a slave as a burden, emphasizing the humane treatment required.
Continuation of the same passage explaining why Israelites should not be treated as slaves—they are God's servants whom He brought out of Egypt.
Contrasts the treatment of Israelite brothers with foreign slaves, stressing the prohibition against ruling harshly over one's brothers.
The prophet Jeremiah refers to the law requiring release of Hebrew slaves every seventh year, which Israel had broken.
Nehemiah confronts the people for selling their brothers into slavery, violating the principle in Leviticus regarding the treatment of poor Israelites.
